In Thomson's plum-pudding model, the electrons and protons of the atom were described as:
options: randomly distributed in a positively charged cloud
orbiting the nucleus in circular paths
clustered at the center of the atom
arranged along the x, y, and z axes
questions.correctAnswer: randomly distributed in a positively charged cloud

questions.question: In 1911, Rutherford tested Thomson's model by aiming positively charged alpha particles at:
options: a thin sheet of gold foil
questions.correctAnswer: a thin sheet of gold foil

questions.question: Most of the alpha particles aimed at the gold foil in Rutherford's experiment:
options: were strongly deflected in every case
bounced back in the opposite direction

questions.question: A few of the alpha particles in Rutherford's experiment were deflected so much that they:
options: went back in the opposite direction
questions.correctAnswer: went back in the opposite direction

questions.question: The strong deflections of alpha particles in the gold foil experiment led to the conclusion that an atom contains a:
options: uniformly spread positive charge like a pudding

options: electrons coming from inside the nucleus
questions.correctAnswer: electrons coming from inside the nucleus

questions.question: Gamma rays are best described as:
options: high-energy rays with no charge that are not affected by electric or magnetic fields
positively charged particles identical to helium nuclei
negatively charged particles deflected by electric fields
questions.correctAnswer: high-energy rays with no charge that are not affected by electric or magnetic fields

questions.question: Radioactivity (radioactive decay) is best defined as:
options: the spontaneous emission of particles and/or radiation from unstable nuclei
the deflection of cathode rays in a magnetic field
the splitting of white light into a spectrum
the emission of light by excited atoms
questions.correctAnswer: the spontaneous emission of particles and/or radiation from unstable nuclei

questions.question: In 1932, James Chadwick showed that when beryllium metal is irradiated with alpha rays, the strongly penetrating radiation produced consists of:
Which statement best describes the neutron?
options: a nuclear particle with a mass almost identical to that of the proton but no electric charge
a positively charged particle identical to the proton
a particle with one negative charge
a particle whose mass is 1840 times that of the proton
questions.correctAnswer: a nuclear particle with a mass almost identical to that of the proton but no electric charge
